decision: Keep the CUDA transfer modes as an opt-in research option of the frame API (fpm_frame_set_transfer_mode, default 0). Mode 3 (lean prepare + lean calls) is the recommended CUDA frame setting for research runs. Defaults, the core and the GUI are unchanged.

hypotheses.H3: held (m3 faster than cpu on 17/17 in every mode; closest Src9 FastMode 0.26 vs 0.30 ms)

failures_and_disclosures.what: mutant pilot before registration: the original T7 (`same = !levels.empty()`) survived
failures_and_disclosures.effect: when the level count shrinks the extra host level is unused (equivalent); when it grows the loop reads past the vector (undefined behaviour) and the tests need not see it
failures_and_disclosures.fix: replaced before registration by T7 = compare width only (a height-only change keeps the old levels) and a test step that changes only the height; the pilot rerun killed it; pilot/mutpilot.log keeps the original result

failures_and_disclosures.effect: about 20 s after the timing step began (round 0, the warm-up round, not in the summary) one poll read formal.log and I listed the log directory; around round 6 the waiting script read formal.log and the last lines of timing.log once; no other connection until the timing finished

failures_and_disclosures.what: lean calls record no timing events
failures_and_disclosures.effect: device_ms is -1 for m2 and m3 in the formal records
failures_and_disclosures.fix: GPU times come from the Nsight runs in profile/

failures_and_disclosures.what: kernel time grows in m3 (Nsight, not formal)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: fineStripes 709 -> 794 us per frame on Src7 and 20.65 -> 22.05 ms on Src6 subpixel, fineNormalize 91 -> 126 us; likely the per-block request load from mapped host memory and the per-thread system fence, not isolated by the arms
failures_and_disclosures.fix: reported; uploading the requests again is a candidate follow-up

failures_and_disclosures.what: m2 not faster on Src4 FastMode (0.89 vs 0.89 ms)
failures_and_disclosures.effect: descriptive arm only; that case has one coarse wait and no fine call

failures_and_disclosures.what: pilot/default.jsonl and pilot/spin.jsonl were written by PowerShell as UTF-16LE with CRLF
failures_and_disclosures.fix: converted to UTF-8 with LF for the archive

ungated_mutants.U1: survived: without the system fence before the barrier the completion value could in principle reach the host before the outputs; on this x86 host PCIe posted writes arrive in order, so no test sees it. The fence stays.
ungated_mutants.U2: survived: without waiting for the previous upload, the next prepare could overwrite host level 0 while its DMA reads it; the CPU copy of each chunk is slower than the previous DMA, so no test sees it. The wait stays.
ungated_mutants.U3: killed: fresh device memory was not zero

limits: one GPU (RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell), one driver (596.71, WDDM), Windows only; the cudaStreamQuery submission and the polling gain may differ under TCC or Linux
frame API only; the handle API is unchanged
polling keeps one CPU core busy while waiting
the single-threaded source copy (about 19 GB/s, Src7 0.64 ms) now dominates prepare on large images
kernels unchanged; no Tensor cores or CUDA Graphs
17 fixed fixtures only; no many-object or 8K scenes
